summary: No new receipt this turn; I checked one thing that looked wrong in the summary view and one that was worth making precise. The apparent problem was not real: the stored Fact does carry all six source anchors and all four receipts (I read state.json directly), so the shortened lists were a display artifact and I did not 'fix' a non-problem. The precision improvement is substantive and comes from receipts already in hand: in both executions that carry the client write (e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 index 5 and 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903 index 7) the stale leader's log end falls from index 12 to 11 after healing while its applied index remains 12 and its FSM still holds six commands against the new leader's five. The truncation therefore removes not only the configuration change at index 11 but also the client command committed and applied at index 12, and the two sides' applied state differs by exactly that command — the client-visible form of the safety violation: an acknowledged write deleted from the log of the node that acknowledged it, with its effect still present only in the divergent FSM. The interpretation now records that explicitly; nothing else changed and no execution is requested.
